mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where the federal funds rate increases by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a strengthening labor market, which typically boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where the unemployment rate drops by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in real estate sales (HOUST) by more than 10% in a month signals a surge in demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where real estate sales increase by more than 10% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where industrial production increases over three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it indicates inflationary pressure during a tightening monetary cycle, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS is above 4% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% in the same month, it signals a robust labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 5% in a month, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2% in the same month, signals strong consumer demand and a healthy labor market, typically leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 5% and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where RSAFS increases by more than 5% and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months signals a weakening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where industrial production declines over three consecutive months.
